name: 7th Angel
description: "7th Angel" opens like a transmission from somewhere just above the city — synth pads bloom into a widescreen sound that feels equal parts cathedral and cockpit, and That Boy Hi Hat rides the estimated 85 BPM groove at a measured, unhurried pace. The catalog mood reads ethereal, uplifting, and cinematic, and the record earns all three: it sounds like a film score that learned to rap, in the vein of the great nocturnal rap soundscapes, recalling the patient grandeur of the alternative rap underground. Bells chime layered underneath the verses, ghostly vocal swells rise in the chorus, and arps trace bright lines throughout the arrangement. An 808 sub bass anchors the low end, hi-hats keep the hypnotic pulse, and ad-libs float like signals from a higher floor. For fans of cinematic rap and dark trap, the 4:00 runtime is euphoric without tipping into saccharine — dreamy, mysterious, and triumphant in the quiet way. That Boy Hi Hat stretches his flow into a near-chant as layers of atmospheric texture stack beneath him, and the major-key lift in the back half opens the track like dawn over the skyline. The mix is studio-polished with real depth, the low tones balanced against the high shimmer. It sits in the catalog apart from the harder post trap cuts, a reminder that the post-trap movement has a ceiling-high sky above it, and the current wave of futuristic rap keeps reaching for this exact altitude. In an alt rap scene obsessed with the ground floor, "7th Angel" looks up — with an alternate mix waiting in the vault for its upcoming release, the record is still ascending.
